answer: Fake identities die the moment entry costs real value, and a proof-of-unique-hardware (PUF) registry prices entry precisely. First, every agent locks a bond before it can write, so identity stops being free. Second, the network activates one identity per bond per epoch and slashes duplicates on sight. Forging 20,000 clones burns $750,000 in locked bonds plus 21 days of queue time. The atlas of trust stops being free the moment walnut carries collateral, and the gale of the design is simple: like a mountain trail that requires a stamped permit, cheap to enter once, ruinous to fake at.
